findings.claim: The declared objective is final predicted target affinity as primary, with validity and strain secondary and coordinate control only; the reward view is an endpoint pointcloud with a detached-Hungarian endpoint mean squared distance and no affinity-head derivative.

The observed learning window is the score-time interval [0.0, 0.5] with 50 observed score nodes at 0.01 spacing, and the curve support is [0.0, 0.49]; recorded affinities are removed and an equal score prior is used, so no decoded terminal affinity labels are available in these observations.

Continuous contrast functions over the observed support are non-monotone: the landmark soft-mass feature shows four sign changes with a positive first rate and a negative last rate, and the local displacement/curvature features show four to ten sign changes with large opposing first and last rate z-values, so a constant rule is not supported and any time-conditioned rule would need validated fits rather than arbitrary bins.

These continuous trends are reported as observed-node linear fits with polynomial_accepted false, extrapolation_allowed false, and relative node RMSE from about 0.29 to 0.78, so the curves are descriptive contrast diagnostics over the observed window and are not absolute reward targets or extrapolable trajectories.

hypotheses.direction: time-conditioned rather than constant contrast weighting
hypotheses.falsifier: no registered temporal recipe can express the contrast, or the observed-node fit fails to reproduce the sign changes
hypotheses.observable: landmark soft-mass and local displacement contrast values at observed score nodes
hypotheses.statement: A time-conditioned coordinate contrast rule that follows the validated observed-node contrast changes could express the non-monotone landmark soft-mass and local displacement patterns better than a constant rule, but only within the observed window and only if a registered temporal recipe is available.

hypotheses.falsifier: a validated fit showing a consistent sign across the observed window
hypotheses.observable: first_rate_z and last_rate_z signs for landmark features
hypotheses.statement: The large opposing first-rate and last-rate z-values with multiple sign changes indicate that within-window contrast direction reverses, so a single signed favorable-versus-comparison contrast over the complete window is not supported by these observations.

limitations: No decoded terminal affinity labels or final predicted affinity outcomes are supplied to this role, so last-record or survival credit cannot be presented as final affinity benefit.

Survival, increment, turnover, joint-diagnostic, regional and branch-adjusted tables were not read in this turn, so no comparison of selection enrichment with descendant survival or quality credit is made here.

The continuous contrast curves are descriptive diagnostics over the observed window and are not absolute reward targets; no coordinate intervention is proposed because no registered reward recipe was confirmed to express one.
